# Implementation plan — Issue #10057: record review findings the editor cannot reach, open one follow-up issue per PR, and stop them from driving more fix rounds

Planning ref: `git rev-parse HEAD` = `ef5287df97f6d1b817aba556fab7dedfb7b5d73e`, branch `main`. Integration branch mismatch: `unknown`. Default-branch reference: `isolated-base`.

## Automation (§20.E)
- **Scripts:** no new script. The work extends:
  - `scripts/review_issue_ledger.sh` (classification and sticky ledger state);
  - `scripts/review_untrusted_workspace.py` (a new read-only `editor-reachable` subcommand built on the existing `allowed()` rule);
  - `scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh` (one follow-up issue call per round);
  - `scripts/collect_pr_check_runs_context.py` (cancelled and timed-out jobs become "no result").

## Where the editor's write limits live (the issue asked the plan to name them)
Today three deterministic rule sets decide what the review editor can write:
1. **Write guard.** `scripts/write_guard.sh` `write_guard_check review_editor <list>` reads `.github/ai/write_guards.v1.json`, phase `review_editor`: `.git/**` is always blocked, and `.github/workflows/**` is blocked unless `ALLOW_WORKFLOW_EDITS=true`. It is called from `scripts/review_commit_changes.sh:301` and `:521`. `review_commit_changes.sh:307-310` also throws away `.github/workflows` changes when `ALLOW_WORKFLOW_EDITS!=true`.
2. **Consumer protected paths.** `scripts/review_commit_changes.sh:502-511`: when `IS_WORKFLOW_SOURCE_REPO!=true`, it unstages `prompts/`, `.github/scripts/`, `.github/prompts/`, `ai-memory/`, `.codex-workflow-src/` and `.codex-workflow-src-main/`.
3. **Sandbox admission.** `scripts/review_untrusted_workspace.py` `allowed(name, commands=…)`, lines 167-193. It refuses excluded components and most dot-directories. `.claude/commands/*.md` and `.claude/docs/*.md` are admitted only when they are in the inventory frozen at `snapshot` time (lines 418-428). This is the rule behind the `.claude/commands/` and test-file cases from #9839, and behind the editor's existing "sandbox-excluded path" answer (`review_apply_fixes.sh:1397`, `:1619`).

## Functions or modules to implement

1. **`scripts/review_untrusted_workspace.py`**
   - Move the inventory computation inside `snapshot()` (lines 419-428) into a helper, `_review_editor_admitted_inventory(host)`. This is a pure move; `snapshot()` calls it and behaves exactly as before.
   - Add a read-only subcommand: `editor-reachable <host> <paths_file> <report_file>`. For each path it writes one line: `reachable<TAB><path>` or `unreachable<TAB><reason-token><TAB><path>`.
     - Reason tokens reuse `_path_rejection_reason()`: `excluded_component`, `dot_directory`, `unsupported_type`, `operator_input`, `live_safety_hook`, `unsafe_name`. A `.claude/commands` or `.claude/docs` path missing from the inventory gets the new token `not_admitted_command`.
     - It never writes to the host and never prints PR-controlled names unescaped. It prints only through `_log_safe_path`.
     - Wire it into `main()` next to `check-paths`.

2. **`scripts/review_issue_ledger.sh`** — new function `classify_unreachable_findings`, run after `FINAL_STATUS` is computed (around lines 925-1000) and before `rewrite_review_issues_without_residuals`.
   - Skip the whole step when `REVIEW_UNREACHABLE_FOLLOWUP_ENABLED` (default `true` in the script itself, §8) is false. Output must then be byte-identical to today's.
   - Collect each current finding's `FILE`. Skip `unknown`, empty, absolute and `..` paths.
   - A finding is unreachable when **any** of these holds:
     - (a) `write_guard_check review_editor` reports `blocked_glob` or `conditional_blocked_glob` for that path, using a temporary single-path list file. The script sources `write_guard.sh` from `SUPPORT_SCRIPTS_DIR`. With `WRITE_GUARDS_ENABLED=false` (bypass), rule (a) never marks anything.
     - (b) `IS_WORKFLOW_SOURCE_REPO!=true` and the path matches the protected-prefix regex copied verbatim from `review_commit_changes.sh:508`. A parity test locks the two copies together.
     - (c) The editor runs in the review sandbox and `editor-reachable` reports `unreachable`. The sandbox condition must be the same one `review_apply_fixes.sh` uses to route the editor into `review_untrusted_sandbox.sh`.
   - **CI exclusion:** a finding is never unreachable when its block text contains the name of a `failed[i]` check from `PR_CHECK_RUNS_CONTEXT_FILE` whose `conclusion` is `failure`, `action_required`, `startup_failure` or `stale`. A failing check on the PR's own head keeps blocking.
   - **Security:** `LENS` is `SECURITY & INPUT VALIDATION` or `IMPLICIT-EXECUTION & TRUST-BOUNDARY RISKS` → `UNREACHABLE_SECURITY: true`.
   - **Sticky state:** an entry whose prior status is `unreachable` stays `unreachable`, does not add to the persist count, and is not re-checked. A new unreachable entry gets status `unreachable` (a new value), plus new entry fields `UNREACHABLE_REASON: <token>` and `UNREACHABLE_SECURITY: true|false`.
   - Extend `normalize_ledger_status` to accept `unreachable`. Rollback is safe: older code maps the unknown value to `PERSISTING`, which is today's behaviour.
   - **Editor input:**
     - A non-security unreachable block is replaced in `review_issues.txt` by a stub `=== UNREACHABLE ISSUE <block> ===` (FILE, LINES, LENS, `STATUS: unreachable`, `LEDGER_ISSUE_ID`, `FOLLOWUP: pending|#N`). This extends `rewrite_review_issues_without_residuals` with a third id file, following the `accepted-residual` stub pattern.
     - A security unreachable block **stays** in the editor input, with an added `UNREACHABLE: security-hold` line.
   - **Handoff file:** write `${RUNTIME_DIR}/review_unreachable_new.tsv` with the newly recorded entries (`issue_id`, `file`, `lines`, `lens`, `security`, `reason`, `block_id`). Write `${RUNTIME_DIR}/review_unreachable_all.tsv` with every unreachable entry, for the PR comment.
   - **Ledger header:** new optional key `UNREACHABLE_FOLLOWUP_ISSUE: <n>`. `parse_prior_ledger` must read it and the header writer (around line 1046) must carry it forward. Existing header and entry keys keep their names (§6/§10).
   - **Log:** add `unreachable:<k>` to the existing `stage=ledger ... transitions=` line. This appends a key; existing keys are untouched.

3. **`scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh`** — new function `review_unreachable_followup_sync`, called right after the ledger stage (after line 1103) and before the editor runs.
   - Read the follow-up number from the ledger header (the marker in the ledger, §15). There is no search call.
   - If there are new entries:
     - With no number: one `gh_retry gh issue create` with label `ai:clarification`, using the same `ensure_label_exists` path as `review_rb_judge.sh:3594-3596`. Title: `Review findings the autofix editor cannot reach — PR #<n>`. Body:
       - one section per finding: cited path, lines, lens, reason, and the reviewer problem text from the block, truncated and fenced (untrusted);
       - `Refs #<pr>` and a link to the PR;
       - marker `<!-- AI_REVIEW_UNREACHABLE_FOLLOWUP pr=<n> -->`.
       - Never an auto-close keyword (§21).
     - With a number: one `gh_retry gh issue comment <N> --body-file` that appends the new findings.
   - Write the number back into the ledger header, and mark recorded entries `UNREACHABLE_FOLLOWUP: #N` so they are never appended twice.
   - Rewrite stub `FOLLOWUP: pending` to `#N`.
   - Write `${RUNTIME_DIR}/review_unreachable_summary.md`.
   - Emit `REVIEW_UNREACHABLE pr=<n> round=<AUTOFIX_ITERATION> findings=<k> followup=<N|none> outcome=recorded|skipped`. Use `skipped` when the switch is off, there are no new entries, or the gh call failed.
   - **Fail-open:** if the gh call fails, the entries stay `unreachable` with `FOLLOWUP: pendin
